nodes.text:
Amber firelight and cool turquoise ritual glows interrupt the deep shadows of a ruined Greco-Roman temple sanctuary. Sun-bleached cream, ochre, and warm brown sandstone carries green oxidation, moss, and sparse ivy. Underfoot, worn multicolored stone tiles and cracked pale slabs are darkened by damp stains, weeds, and age.

A massive twisted, moss-covered dead tree dominates the long, sunken rectangular courtyard. Chains and skull ornaments hang from the central tree; candles, bones, pottery, and offerings surround its roots. Several substantial temple buildings and roofless colonnaded halls rise one to two monumental levels around the court, facing inward across broad staircases, raised walkways, balustrades, bridges, and narrow passages.

Tall fluted columns, carved entablatures, monumental arches, statue niches, and heavy masonry stand amid collapsed upper walls, broken colonnades, and partially buried chambers. Sightlines grow layered and cramped. Fallen column drums, capitals, masonry, and rotting beams lie heaped around the ruins, completing the dense, atmospheric sanctuary.
